Introduction/Context  
Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)–induced myositis (irMyositis) occurs in ~1% of patients treated with anti–PD-1 or anti–CTLA-4 and can be severe or fatal. Here, NanoString PanCancer Immune profiling of skeletal muscle biopsies was used to compare gene expression between irMyositis, two spontaneous dermatomyositis (DM) subtypes (anti-Mi2 and anti-TIF1-γ), and non-diseased controls (NDC). Differential expression results (adj.P.Val < 0.05) were preranked by log₂FC and analyzed by preranked GSEA against Reactome_Pathways_2024.

Analysis  
Across both DM subtypes versus NDC, a canonical interferon signature (Interferon Signaling, Interferon α/β) and antigen-presentation modules (MHC class I, cross-presentation, TLR cascades) were nearly unanimously upregulated (100% in Mi2, ~98% in TIF1γ). In contrast, when comparing irMyositis to either DM subtype, those same interferon-driven pathways were among the most significantly *down*regulated (5/5 top hits in irMyositis vs Mi2; 4/5 in irMyositis vs TIF1γ). Conversely, irMyositis showed *up* enrichment of TNF-receptor binding and T-cell receptor activation pathways (e.g., “TNFs Bind Their Physiological Receptors,” “Phosphorylation of CD3 and TCR Zeta Chains,” “Costimulation by the CD28 Family”), which were not top hits in DM vs NDC. These results point to a shift from an interferon-dominant inflammation in spontaneous DM toward a TNF- and T-cell-centric immunopathology in ICI-induced myositis.

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate by plotting leading‐edge expression (e.g., MX1, ISG15, CD3E, TNFRSF8) across all samples.  
2. Perform orthogonal over-representation analysis (ORA) on the same preranked gene lists to confirm pathway directionality.  
3. Investigate upstream drivers (e.g., PD-1/CTLA-4 engagement levels) and ligand expression in muscle tissue to connect checkpoint blockade to TNF/TCR signaling.  
4. Assess single-cell or spatial transcriptomics to localize T cells versus myocytes and determine whether TCR engagement is direct or via antigen-presenting cells.
